newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-COURIER RALLIES FROM TWO SETS DOWN TO GIVE U.S. 2-0 LEAD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COURIER RALLIES FROM TWO SETS DOWN TO GIVE U.S. 2-0 LEAD.

text.p: Jim Courier rallied from two sets down to beat Jan Siemerink 4-6 4-6 6-1 7-6 (7-4) 6-3 on Friday to give the United States a 2-0 lead over the Netherlands in their Davis Cup quarter-final tie.
Courier needed three hours, 24 minutes to overcome Siemerink and put the Americans within one victory of reaching the semifinals.
In the opening singles, Andre Agassi won his 14th straight Davis Cup match, pounding out a 7-6 (8-6) 6-4 7-6 (7-2) hardcourt win over Sjeng Schalken in windy conditions at the Palisades Tennis Club.

The Americans can wrap up the best-of-five tie Saturday in doubles when Rick Leach and Jonathan Stark meet Dutchmen Jacco Eltingh and Paul Haarhuis. A win would put the United States into the semifinals against either Australia or the Czech Republic.
The rousing, comeback victory marked a first for Courier. The two-time French and Australian Open champion had never before recovered from a two-set deficit in tour play or in Davis Cup competition.

Siemerink, displaying an effective lefthanded serve and volley game, pinned Courier to the baseline as he raced out to a two-sets to love lead. But the American did not panic and begin to wear down the Dutchmen with his aggressive ground game.

Siemerink grabbed a 3-1 lead in the fourth set and served for the set at 5-4. But Courier fought him off to force a tiebreaker, which he eventually won to even the match when Siemerink netted a backhand approach.
The climactic fifth set was on serve at 3-3 before Courier ran off the final three games, including the decisive break in the ninth game to go ahead 5-4.

Agassi, who has been mired in a bad slump, got the United States off to a good start as he rose to the occasion yet again in the Davis Cup. The Las Vegas showman improved to 23-4 in the team competition with his victory over Schalken.

Schalken battled back from a 4-0 deficit in the first set before losing in a tiebreak. In the third set, the Dutch baseliner built a 5-3 lead by breaking Agassi three times, but Agassi charged back to force another tiebreaker.
Agassi seized a 5-0 lead in the decider on his way to clinching the match as Schalken sailed a backhand and then a forehand beyond the baseline.
